query: Across Type of Traveller and Class, which review themes are associated with higher vs. lower Overall Rating?

per_column.name: crew_service_warmth
per_column.rationale: Extracts a qualitative crew-warmth theme with three clean, well-separated levels (warm_attentive / professional_neutral / inattentive_rushed) plus a small NULL. This is an external associational dimension one can segment on and cross-tabulate against Overall Rating within Traveller/Class groups. It decomposes the free-text review into a theme rather than restating the numeric focus.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_design
per_column.rationale: Interpretable ordered categories (spacious_comfortable / adequate / cramped_uncomfortable) that can be grouped and compared to Overall Rating. High NULL share (~40%, reviews not mentioning seats) modestly weakens coverage, but the non-null categories are clear and well-separated, so meaningful comparison is possible.

per_column.name: food_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: Three legible quality tiers (excellent_tasty / adequate_acceptable / poor_bland) usable for segmentation against the focus. Like seat comfort it carries a large NULL block (~47%), but the coded values remain interpretable and support theme-vs-rating exploration.

per_column.name: aircraft_condition_age
per_column.rationale: Adds a genuinely new dimension absent from the original schema (aircraft modernity/condition) with clean levels (modern_well_maintained / adequate_acceptable / old_dated). Well-separated, interpretable, and directly groupable against Overall Rating — a strong EDA variable.

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Distinct service-responsiveness theme with four interpretable, well-separated categories. Some conceptual overlap with crew warmth, but it captures a separate responsiveness axis and is a valid, human-readable segmentation to compare against ratings.

per_column.name: value_perception_premium
per_column.rationale: Value-perception theme with meaningful, well-separated levels (excellent_value / fair_price_justified / overpriced_for_experience / premium_not_delivered). It is highly correlated with overall satisfaction and partially echoes the existing Value For Money field, so it edges toward near-restatement, but as a coded theme it still supports interpretable segmentation and is retained as a predictor.

per_column.name: service_consistency_across_class
per_column.rationale: Directly targets the query's Class dimension: legible categories (consistent_high / class_appropriate / two_tier_disparity / degraded_economy) let an explorer relate cross-class service consistency to Overall Rating. Well-separated and highly relevant to the stated intent.

per_column.name: special_requests_accommodation
per_column.rationale: New accommodation theme with clear, well-separated categories (personalized_attentive / standard_adequate / inflexible_no_accommodation / refused_discriminatory) and negligible NULLs. Fully groupable and interpretable for comparison against the focus.

judge.rationale: As a set, the columns realise the EDA claim well: they decompose free-text reviews into eight interpretable, well-separated thematic dimensions, each of which can be grouped/segmented and cross-tabulated against Overall Rating within Type of Traveller and Class strata — exactly matching 'which review themes are associated with higher vs. lower Overall Rating.' None are opaque scores; all use human-readable, mutually distinct category labels rather than fine-grained or near-constant values, and none merely restate the numeric focus. Minor deductions: several themes (seat, food, value, crew) partly overlap with existing numeric rating fields, value_perception_premium borders on near-restatement of overall satisfaction, and three columns carry ~35–47% NULLs that reduce comparison coverage. Overall this is a coherent, informative set for relationship discovery.
